Number of studies.evidence_source: The section describes Malay female and Malay male subsamples within the same analyses (e.g., "For the Malay female subsample (n = 149) ..." and "For the Malay male subsample (n=157) ..." and "we assessed the degree of factor similarity across the Malay female and male subsamples ..."), indicating a single study with two subsamples.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports exploratory factor analyses of the BAS-2 for Malay female (n = 149) and Malay male (n = 157) subsamples. Parallel analysis indicated a single factor for the female subsample (first eigenvalue 5.45 > random 3.28) explaining 54.5% of variance and a single factor for the male subsample (eigenvalue 4.98) explaining 49.83% of variance; omega for the 10-item BAS-2 was .88 in both subsamples. Tucker's congruence coefficient = .85 suggests similar but not identical factor structures across the two subsamples.
section_summary.evidence_source: "For the Malay female subsample (n = 149), ... only the first factors from the actual data had λ greater than the criterion λ generated from the random data (i.e., 5.45 [actual data] compared to 3.28 [random data]). ... As such, we retained a single factor, which explained 54.5% of the common variance. ... Omega for all 10 BAS-2 items in this subsample was .88 (95% CI = .86-.91)." "For the Malay male subsample (n=157), ... This factor had an λ = 4.98 and explained 49.83% of the common variance in the data. ... Omega for the 10-item BAS-2 total score this subsample was .88 (95% CI = .86–.91)." "Finally, we assessed the degree of factor similarity across the Malay female and male subsamples using Tucker's congruence coefficient, which was .85 and suggested similar but not equal factor structures."
